name: The Post Office at Chicago
trade: the United States post office at Chicago

staff.name: John S. C. Hogan
staff.basis: 'John S. C. Hogan, Postmaster, came in 1832' — Andreas, and the resident card carries the same office attested at the same citation. He succeeded Bailey on 2 November 1832 and holds the office across the scene date; the `from` on this row is that appointment and not the office's own opening.

locations.basis: NOT HOGAN'S STORE, AND THAT IS THE READING THIS RECORD EXISTS TO CARRY. The office was in hogan_store from 31 March 1831 until about July 1834, when Andreas has it removed 'to near the corner of Franklin and South Water', where it stayed through Hogan's term — so on 1835-07-01 it is on South Water Street at the Franklin end. The committed structure record hogan_store already states this in its own `function` note, and the walkthrough's `first_post_office` anchor marks where the mail BEGAN, not where it was taken on the scene date.
locations.limit_reason: THE BUILDING IS NOT MODELLED AND WOULD BE ALMOST ENTIRELY INVENTION. hogan_store's research note puts it about 100 m east of that building and says that nothing reached describes its construction, its size or its side of either street; docs/RESEARCH/hogan_store.md § 4 states the same refusal. AND THE CORNER ITSELF CARRIES A LIVE CONFLICT (T-0859): eight printings of Hogan's standing card, from 13 August 1834 through the issue of 1 July 1835, put his South Water store 'one door [… of] the Post Office', and one door is not four blocks from Franklin. The conflict is recorded and not resolved here; the street is what both readings agree on, so the street is as far as this location goes.

dates.basis: The office, not the building: Chicago's post office was established on 31 March 1831 and is still taking the mail on the scene date. It moved rooms about July 1834 — that move is on the location's `from` — and a moved office is the same establishment.

proprietor_community.basis: This record names nobody the resident layer holds a card for, so there is no person to read a community off. The silence is in the register.

replaceable_by: A printing or a plat that names the building at Franklin and South Water, or that settles which door of it Hogan's store stood from — either would close T-0859's conflict and could seat this record on a roof.
